findings.failure_scenario: details.token.balanceParsed is normalized through safeNumberString (kit-bg/src/vaults/impls/evm/sdkEvm/utils.ts), which returns BigNumber.toString(); bignumber.js 9.1.2 emits exponential form for exponents <= -7, so a balance like 0.0000001 becomes "1e-7". Tapping Max calls onChangeAmountValue("1e-7") and the regex ^$|^0(\.\d{0,N})?$|^[1-9]\d*(\.[0-9]{0,N})?$|^[1-9]\d*\.$|^0\.$ fails, so the amount is never set and no error is shown — before this change, new BigNumber("1e-7") parsed fine and the input was filled (countDecimalPlaces returns 0 for it, so the old overflow check also passed it). The identical gate was added to ApproveBaseStake (index.tsx:137), UniversalClaim (index.tsx:94) and UniversalWithdraw (index.tsx:162); pasting "1,000" or "01.5" is likewise silently dropped now.
findings.summary: The new validateAmountInput regex gate silently rejects numeric strings the previous BigNumber-based handler accepted (exponent notation such as "1e-7", comma-separated or leading-zero values), so the Max button becomes a silent no-op for small balances.

findings.failure_scenario: The same change translates "earn.approve_deposit"/"earn.approve_permit"/"global.try_again" into each language (e.g. zh_CN: "授权并认购") but adds "Limit.expire_day": "Day", "Limit.order_status_open": "Open", "prime.app_data": "App data", "prime.last_update": "Last update" as English in all 18 non-English JSONs (verified with grep across all 19 files). A Chinese or Japanese user running the app in their locale will see "Day/Days/Hour/.../Unfilled" and "App data"/"Last update" in English as soon as code renders the ETranslations.Limit_* / prime_* enum members that this diff also wires into the enum — inconsistent with the fully translated remainder of each file.
findings.summary: The diff adds 24 new locale keys (all 22 "Limit.*" keys, "prime.app_data", "prime.last_update") with untranslated English values into every non-English locale file, so non-English users will see English text for these strings.

findings.failure_scenario: aprValue = "0.0045": Number(aprValue) > 0 passes the guard, but formatApy (Staking/components/utils.tsx) computes new BigNumber("0.0045").decimalPlaces(2, ROUND_DOWN).toFixed(2) = "0.00", so the staking entry on the token detail page shows "Up to 0.00% in annual rewards" instead of the previous "Up to 0.0045% in annual rewards", misleading users about staking returns for low-APR tokens.
findings.summary: formatApy floors the APR to 2 decimals with ROUND_DOWN, so any token with a positive APR below 0.01% now renders as "Up to 0.00% in annual rewards", reading as zero rewards.

findings.failure_scenario: User approves "1.0" (ref["1.0"] = true, allowance updates, isApprove becomes false, progress shows "1. Approve ✓ 2. Deposit"); the user then edits the amount to "1" (same value) — showStakeProgressRef.current["1"] is undefined and allowance covers it, so the progress indicator silently vanishes mid-flow. Conversely, showStakeProgressRef.current[amountValue] = true is set before navigationToTxConfirm, so a cancelled approval permanently marks the key. Also, when the page opens with sufficient allowance (isApprove false from the start, e.g. a previously approved spender), isShowStakeProgress is false forever and the StakeProgress that previously always rendered at the deposit step is now hidden for the whole flow.
findings.summary: Stake progress visibility is keyed on the exact amount input string in a never-cleared ref, so the completed-approve state is lost when the user reformats the same numeric amount, and the progress indicator no longer renders at all in the deposit-only flow.

findings.failure_scenario: ProviderInfo({ ..., babylonStakingCap, poolFee }) no longer uses poolFee anywhere after the GridItem removal, while ProviderSection still executes `if (details.provider.poolFee) { providerProps.poolFee = { value: details.provider.poolFee }; }` (lines 201-203) and IProviderInfoProps still declares poolFee. .eslintrc.js sets '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars' to 'error' outside dev mode, and poolFee sits after the last used argument (babylonStakingCap), so production lint fails on the unused destructured parameter; the prop plumbing is dead code for future maintainers.
findings.summary: Removing the poolFee GridItem left poolFee destructured but unused in ProviderInfo while ProviderSection still builds and passes it, leaving dead plumbing and an unused-variable lint error.

findings.failure_scenario: After `if (!validateAmountInput(value, decimals)) return;` at line 141, any value reaching line 151 has at most `decimals` fractional digits (regex \d{0,decimal}), so `countDecimalPlaces(value) > decimals` can never be true — the `setAmountValue((oldValue) => oldValue)` branch is dead, and when decimals is undefined the `decimals &&` short-circuit also skips it. The same dead branch remains in ApproveBaseStake (line ~146-152), UniversalClaim (line ~104-110) and UniversalWithdraw (line ~172-178); the codebase would be simpler with the redundant check removed, and each file still imports countDecimalPlaces solely for it.
findings.summary: The pre-existing countDecimalPlaces overflow check is now unreachable dead code in all four staking amount handlers because the added regex gate already caps fractional digits at `decimals`, and the Swap-view-local util import is kept alive only by that dead branch.
